43770.Description: This trout species somehow survives in the stagnant, waste-filled sediment of the driftdowns. Unsurprisingly, its highly polluted flesh is entirely unsuitable for consumption.

43771.Name: Electrobetta
43771.Description: This elegant wavekin is wreathed in an eerie purple glow. Naturalists have observed the species ingesting small waterborne fragments of electrope, and speculate that the resultant buildup of electrical charge is responsible for the luminance.

43772.Name: Thundering Redbelly
43772.Description: Come spawning season, this usually unremarkable brown fish undergoes a dazzling visual change. The poetic scholar who named this wavekin likened its vibrant stripes to flashes of lightning during a calamitous thunderstorm.

43773.Name: Yyasulani Bowfin
43773.Description: Hailing from a time long before Yyasulani was blighted by the dome's presence, this well-camouflaged wavekin can be found lurking in waters with a potent lightning charge.

43774.Name: Crackling Flounder
43774.Description: With its faint turquoise glow, this charming flounder is said to rival the most precious of gems in terms of sheer beauty. Unfortunately, given the hazardous environment it inhabits, getting close enough to marvel at this fish is rarely worth the risk to life and limb.

43775.Name: Goldgrouper
43775.Description: A resplendent golden wavekin found amongst the submerged ruins of Alexandria. The excess lightning energy that permeates the area has imbued its scales with metallic strength and a chrome-like sheen.

43776.Name: Everkeep Yabby
43776.Description: This crustacean is found in waterways throughout Everkeep. A culinary favorite, steamed yabby is often paired with a variety of colorful but questionable sauces.

43777.Name: Stickleback
43777.Description: The row of pointed spines that adorn this wavekin's back act as a deterrent to predators. Incidentally, the appellation “stickleback” is used to deride the startling fashion choices made by wayward youths.

43778.Name: Custodian Carp
43778.Description: An unabashed omnivore, this wavekin will happily consume whatever it can fit inside its mouth. Hoping to capitalize on this unfussy approach to feeding─and thereby get rid of unwanted pests─cleaners have released several specimens into the artificial ponds of Solution Nine's residential sector.

43779.Name: Mosaic Loach
43779.Description: The pattern covering this streamlined fish resembles a smattering of multicolored pebbles. It is unclear whether its name derives from this coloration, or from it being a firm favorite among employees at Solution Nine's premier café.

43780.Name: Rosebud Frog
43780.Description: Legend has it that this amphibian first emerged into the world from a red rosebud. Given the species' love of nectar, scholars have surmised that whoever was responsible for the tale simply misinterpreted the sight of a young frog enjoying a fragrant meal.

43781.Name: Knight Goby
43781.Description: This valorous wavekin is the national fish of Alexandria. Revered as a symbol of loyalty, its silver scales invite comparisons to the realm's armored knights.

43782.Name: Windspath Eel
43782.Description: Readily identified by the faintly unsettling eye-like markings that adorn their tails, wild specimens are usually light brown. In the abnormally pure waters of Windspath Gardens, however, this eel has developed a muted, almost transparent hue.

43783.Name: Harlequin Lancer
43783.Description: The black and yellow splotches that cover this wavekin's body bring to mind the gaudy costumes of clowns and jesters. Yet far from serving to entertain, these vibrant colors warn predators that the lancer's flesh is filled with deadly toxins.

43784.Name: Cleyran Carp
43784.Description: This jet black carp is one of a few surviving specimens from Cleyra. Sadly, many other wavekin native to the region now exist only as entries in textbooks and scholarly journals.

43785.Name: Giant Snakehead
43785.Description: Possessing primitive lungs, this sizable fish is often seen surfacing for air. When observing such behavior, even the most experienced naturalists have been known to mistake its blunt head for that of a scalekin.

43786.Name: Datnioides
43786.Description: The young fry of these striped predators are highly susceptible to aetheric fluctuations─a phenomenon which manifests itself in their vibrant scales. As the species matures, this susceptibility wanes, along with the coloration.

43787.Name: Neo Arowana
43787.Description: Native to a now-lost realm, this species' survival is credited to Alexandrian hobbyists who bred the fish for its iridescent appearance.

43788.Name: Canal Bream
43788.Description: This wavekin was a popular source of food in the port settlement Canal Town was based on. It is said that young chefs tasked with filleting the fish were often put off by its large, posthumously watchful eyes.

43789.Name: Iris Wrasse
43789.Description: In the past, Endless would flock to the balustrades for a glimpse of these vibrant shoaling fish in the canals, likening their flowing form to a wildflower meadow astir in the wind.

43790.Name: Canal Drum
43790.Description: In days gone by, the thoroughfares of Canal Town would often be thronged with crowds watching one of the resort's many musical troupes. This rounded wavekin takes its name from the drums used in such performances. Appellation aside, tapping out a triplet or two on its scales is discouraged.

43791.Name: Butterfly Ray
43791.Description: This elongated oval ray looks like an oversized butterfly come to rest with its wings unfurled. Referencing the wavekin's color, some needlessly petty naturalists insist that it actually bears closer resemblance to a moth.

43792.Name: Hydro Louvar
43792.Description: Favoring warm, temperate waters, this wavekin once roamed oceans far and wide. Sadly, its present habitat rather curtails these migratory tendencies.

43793.Name: Devotion Clam
43793.Description: A beige bivalve originally hailing from a region of expansive shallows. This highly nutritious and exquisitely flavorsome creature was once a frequent fixture on dining tables across Alexandria.

43794.Name: Forgotten One
43794.Description: The Meso Terminal contains nary a record on this fish, nor the circumstances surrounding its introduction to the resort. The whys, hows, and wheres of its existence are a mystery that will likely persist forevermore.

43795.Name: Copper Shark
43795.Description: Relatives of this gargantuan rust-tinged shark voraciously stalk their prey in temperate seas. This particular species is comparatively docile, and seems content to trawl the waters of Living Memory for plankton and other microbial organisms.

43796.Name: Golden Day
43796.Description: This wavekin and its dull golden scales has become a symbol of nostalgic reminiscence─calling to mind the faded glory of bygone days. Despite the somber association, the sight of this charming fish has soothed many an onlooker over the years.

43797.Name: Starglass Gibel
43797.Description: Glinting with a starry luster, this fish takes its name from the Yesterland plaza. Bereft of a natural night sky, people would turn their gaze to the waterways and watch these graceful wavekin float and frolic, inventing new constellations based on their positions in the current.

43798.Name: Scarlet Queen
43798.Description: This beautiful, selectively bred species was awarded to the royal family upon Queen Sphene's resurrection as an Endless.

43799.Name: Ultimoat Carp
43799.Description: This large wavekin was once a domineering presence in Alexandria's castle moat. When the realm was reborn as Proto Alexandria, the few remaining carp also found themselves enjoying a new lease on life.

44339.Name: Icuvlo's Barter
44339.Description: Bearing the name of the Pelu god of wealth, this tiny amphibian is said to guide travelers to the fabled golden city. This association likely comes from the toxin secreted by the frog, which induces a debilitating sensitivity to light, giving the world around the victim a dazzling gilded sheen.

44340.Name: Moongripper
44340.Description: On moonlit nights, this crustacean lifts its mighty pincers aloft, reaching out as if to pluck the pockmarked satellite right out of the sky. According to Yok Huy legend, specimens that successfully grasp the moon's image in their claws grow to be stronger and larger than their counterparts.

44341.Name: Cazuela Crab
44341.Description: Considered a delicacy by the Hanuhanu, the preferred method of preparing this weighty crustacean is to simply place it atop a boiling cookpot and steam the crab, carapace and all.

44343.Name: Ilyon Asoh Cichlid
44343.Description: This beautiful, vibrant wavekin is beloved by the Xbr'aal, and, in times past, was enshrined as a deity in Ilyon Asoh. So profound was the villagers' reverence that they saw fit to ban fishing for the divine creature on all but a handful of days each year.

44342.Name: Stardust Sleeper
44342.Description: Although known to also inhabit the Stardust Sea, this secretive wavekin favors the deep, briny waters of Xty'iinbek Tsoly. As such, sightings are few and far between.

44345.Name: Hwittayoanaan Cichlid
44345.Description: Among the several species of cichlid native to the region, this particular specimen is often seen in the waters closest to the Boughs of Hwittayoanaan. Naturalists have posited that the wavekin's heightened olfactory senses lure it towards the Hhetsarro's open-air burial grounds.

44346.Name: Thunderswift Trout
44346.Description: Deftly navigating the detritus-strewn waters at impossible speeds, there is nary an ilm of the driftdowns safe from this fearsome fish.

44344.Name: Pixel Loach
44344.Description: Reminiscent of the display panels utilized throughout Everkeep, the intricate patterns adorning this wavekin shift and shimmer as it swims. When exposed to an electrical current, these markings cycle through an exuberant myriad of colors, much to the delight of any onlookers.

44347.Name: Cloudsail
44347.Description: With its oversized dorsal fin and aerodynamic snout, this wavekin can be glimpsed soaring through the mists betwixt Yok and Xak Tural. Much like the clouds that blanket its natural habitat, the flesh of this toothsome fish is light and fluffy, making it a popular ingredient in a variety of local dishes.

44334.Name: Oily Ropefish
44334.Description: This wavekin secretes a coat of oily mucus that allows it to adapt to subtle changes in water temperature, and is prized by artisans for its utility in the production of heavy-duty lubricants.

44335.Name: Yak Awak Core
44335.Description: Found in the depths of Yak Awak Tsoly, these twinkling spheroid creatures are a valuable (if somewhat dim) light source for the people of the Ut'ohmu Horizon.

44336.Name: Inktopus
44336.Description: Like many octopodes, this wavekin hides in a cloud of its own ink when threatened. After sailors noticed that this particular ink left a nearly permanent stain upon everything it touched, it was soon adopted for use in nautical mapmaking.

44337.Name: Honeycomb Sponge
44337.Description: This aquatic invertebrate was named for the hexagonal pores in its spongin mesh. Once its living cells have been cruelly stripped away, its skeletal remains can be used to create luxurious lathers with the soap of one's choice.

44338.Name: Cenote Oyster
44338.Description: The thick shell of this wavekin, found only in saltwater cenotes, is pulverized and added to soil to improve its drainage. Historically, this has saved countless structures from damage during heavy rain.

47988.Name: Cabinkeep Permit
47988.Description: Compared to its timid lesser brethren, this wavekin is bestowed with a positively brazen temperament, and is often spotted leading shoals around the shallows near the For'ard Cabins with a self-assured grace. Guests have likened its presence to that of a conscientious, well-versed caretaker.

47989.Name: Muttering Matamata
47989.Description: As pleated matamata age, their shells continue to grow indefinitely. According to legend, the largest and most ancient specimens eventually fuse with the landscape, blocking rivers in the process─the once-mighty roar of water reduced to a mere muttering. Though naturalists have yet to observe the phenomena in the wild, this specimen renders the tales believable.

47990.Name: Riverlong Candiru
47990.Description: Capable of singlehandedly reducing the largest of predators to naught but a pile of polished bones, this wavekin combines the voraciousness of its kin with an independent tenacity that is chilling to behold.

47991.Name: Deep Canopy
47991.Description: The rhomboid form of this pale yellow fish closely resembles fallen foliage. Indeed, local folklore tells of leaves borne on the wind morphing into wavekin after alighting on the surface of the Iq Br'aax reservoir.

47992.Name: Awaksbane Apoda
47992.Description: Despite being considerably larger than other apoda, this ancient amphibian's chief form of defense remains the same: secreting a highly toxic slime. Unlike its smaller cousins, however, it produces toxins in such quantities as to blight the waters of the tsoly it calls home.

47993.Name: Ttokatoa
47993.Description: The dense black roe laid by this wavekin sink down to the substrate where it spends much of its time. Known in the Hhetsarro tongue as the “swallower of dawn,” to witness this wavekin's gaping maw loom up from the depths of Lake Toari is to keenly understand the origins of its name.

47994.Name: Thunderous Flounder
47994.Description: When the scales of this flat fish catch the light, they appear to coruscate with electrical energy. This startling effect is all the more pronounced when lightning strikes nearby.

47995.Name: Harlequin Queen
47995.Description: Routinely observed leading retinues of harlequin lancers with magnanimous poise, this regal wavekin lashes out with its venomous barbels to fell prey with deadly precision.

46188.Name: Goldentail
46188.Description: Struck daily by the lightning that pours into the crackling canyons, this eel is valued for its delicate-yet-flavorful flesh that notably numbs the tongue with an electrifying spiciness.

46249.Name: Purple Palate
46249.Description: It is believed that in the basin's pristine depths, the currents churned by Ku'uxage's falls transform themselves into aether-rich wavekin. Thus does the purple palate surely share the refined tastes of its Ku'uxage parent-waters' grand “tongue.”

46779.Name: Sunray Ray
46779.Description: This carefree ray lives happily amongst the clouds, guided only by the wind and its own sense of adventure. Not even capture can unsettle its insouciance, as it tends to bond with the fisher that reels it in.

46189.Name: Prime Adjudicator
46189.Description: With a lifespan that exceeds even that of Yok Huy, this enormous wavekin commands the depths of Karvarhur the First while robed in thick swaths of lichen that bespeak its ancient legacy.

46190.Name: Crenicichla Miyaka
46190.Description: This large specimen of crenicichla dominates the shoreline waters of Miyakabek'zoma, boasting the elegant and unmarred fins of an absolute victor.

46191.Name: Iron Shadowtongue
46191.Description: While the skins of related species can be processed into armor, the sable scales of this primordial wavekin boast even greater toughness, and are sturdy enough to substitute as weaponry without alteration.

46192.Name: Lotl-in-waiting
46192.Description: Said to spring forth from sunbeams as radiant droplets, these wavekin are worth their weight in gold, for they have long been considered the ideal gift to ingratiate oneself with those in high places.

46193.Name: Azure Diver
46193.Description: This acrobatic wavekin is often seen leaping skyward before plummeting straight and true into the mists it calls home. On one occasion, a particularly dextrous specimen found itself the target of a mysterious traveler's probing spear tip. Predicting a swift skewering, onlookers were instead treated to a dazzling aerial display as the creature nimbly evaded defeat.

46194.Name: Sprouting Perch
46194.Description: On closer inspection, the speckled markings that adorn this wavekin are actually bud-like protrusions. Any fish lured close by the apparition of a sprouting buffet usually find themselves on the menu instead.

46195.Name: Gigagiant Snakehead
46195.Description: Boasting a cavernous set of lungs proportionate to their gargantuan size, these fish have been recorded subsisting on a single lungful of air before breaching the surface again. It is difficult to assess which is more impressive─the wavekin's physical attributes, or the patience of the naturalists who waited for days on end to make such an observation.

46196.Name: Gondola Louvar
46196.Description: This saltwater fish can be found languidly roaming the waterways of Canal Town, shoals of lesser wavekin in tow. To exert control over its territory, it plies the same routes back and forth with the consistency of a commercial ferry service.

49794.Name: Purse of Riches
49794.Description: Clad in glinting golden scales, these substantial wavekin resemble pouches laden with coin. Those fooled by the illusion often dive into the water after glimpsing the fish, visions of wealth soon vanishing with the creature's retreating form.

49795.Name: Punutiy Pain
49795.Description: Although known to primarily target hapless peddlers and other waterside wanderers, with increased punutiy traffic in the region, these voracious carnivores now enjoy a more varied diet─much to the chagrin of the punutiy handlers and their gentle charges.

49796.Name: Shuckfin Dace
49796.Description: Some scholars have likened this wavekin's form to an ear of corn. Indeed, the sight of these fish basking in the sun with their silk-like tailfins aquiver is akin to that of a golden field, ripe kernels ready to harvest.

49797.Name: Shin Snuffler
49797.Description: A species of flat catfish residing in the shallow waters of Ankledeep. Locals wading in are often met with the tickling touch of barbels as the pool's residents greet their shins with cautious interest.

49798.Name: Moxutural Greatgar
49798.Description: Presiding over Cenote Moxutural with an apparent sense of ownership, this mighty gar once frolicked with local residents. Since the nearby village fell silent, however, it has kept a lonesome vigil in the depths.

49799.Name: Heirloom Goldgrouper
49799.Description: This golden wavekin is found in the deepest recesses beyond the submerged skyline. Infused with lightning energy, it wreaths itself in scraps of metal, darting through the water in a flash of scale and steel.

49800.Name: Datnioides Aeroplanos
49800.Description: In certain lights, this striped predator appears iridescent, its coloration shifting and shimmering as if stirred by the wind.

49801.Name: Esperance Carp
49801.Description: These large and lively specimens are descended from the wavekin that once dwelled in Alexandria's castle moat. Eager to see the population flourish, naturalists chose to enshrine their hope in the naming of the fish.

51999.Name: Ole Ole Ole
51999.Description: Though the name may suggest to Eorzean speakers some association with the leftward direction, rest assured that, unlike its smaller kin, this specimen can only swim toward its right fin. Its appellation instead refers to a chant beloved by fans of a local ball-based sport─who must resist the temptation to send it soaring aloft.

52000.Name: Iron Oxydoras
52000.Description: Much like its lesser brethren, this formidable fish has a long history of being brandished as a blunt instrument. In the days of Yok Huy conquest, warriors encountering these wavekin in Kozama'uka would snatch the creatures from the shallows, thereby acquiring slippery─and presumably perturbed─cudgels with which to wage war.

52001.Name: Excavator Catfish
52001.Description: This large freshwater fish uses its tapered, shovel-like snout to probe the riverbed, hunting for tasty morsels amidst the mud.

52002.Name: Moonmarking Saucer
52002.Description: The flat forms of these wavekin are held to wax and wane in perfect harmony with the moon. In the depths of the Ja Tiika Heartland, where the night sky is shrouded by unbroken canopy, people have long used these creatures as a kind of living calendar.

52003.Name: Autarch's Supper
52003.Description: Revered for their role in maintaining the cleanliness of water sources, these slender wavekin are considered symbols of good fortune in Mamook. Such is the reverence for these fortuitous fish that they are traditionally served at the weaning ceremonies of two-headed Mamool Ja infants.

52004.Name: Bitterbark Caiman
52004.Description: These hulking scalekin spend much of their lives in murky brackish waters, flesh slowly steeping in salt. So delicious a prize are these pre-seasoned creatures, hunters will gladly risk life and limb to bring one down.

52005.Name: Vagrant Keeper
52005.Description: Appearing out of nowhere, borne on sudden, ever-shifting air currents, these tunicates are widely feared as spectral messengers from the dark depths of Zorgor─not to mention their penchant for grabbing the ankles of unwary passersby.

52006.Name: Shined Copper Shark
52006.Description: This gargantuan shark gleams with the brilliance of burnished copper. Some believe this luster results from a diet rich in Endless and their aether.

51209.Name: First Mate's Finger
51209.Description: Owing to its green-tinged carapace and digit-like shape, Roegadyn sailors who spot one of these creatures floundering on deck will invariably ask their fellow countrymen if anyone is missing a finger. That the joke endures is less a testament to its hilarity, and more an indication that encounters with the crustacean remain a rare novelty.

51210.Name: Specterfish
51210.Description: Many sailors consider these fish to be an ill omen, likening their pallid, shimmering forms to the souls of those lost at sea. Such superstition is easily derided─until one witnesses the chilling sight of these nigh ethereal creatures undulating beneath the waves.

51211.Name: Rhotano Permit
51211.Description: One of the many permit species that thrive in waters from Eorzea to Tural. This particular variety is notably itinerant, and is known for migrating in accordance with seasonal currents.

51229.Name: Red Mantis
51229.Description: Often mistaken for common shrimp, these red-shelled crustaceans can make deft use of their scythe-like front legs.

51230.Name: Datli Gwl
51230.Description: In the old tongue of Thavnair, this handsome crab's name means “sweet rose.” Although naturally poisonous, a judicious boiling will neutralize the toxins, providing for a safe, delectable feast.

51231.Name: Agama's Strand
51231.Description: Said to have started life as a fallen strand of Saint Agama's hair, the dried forms of these wavekin are often seen adorning worshipers' garments like parched little talismans.

51212.Name: Rhotano Dahlia
51212.Description: This stinging anemone inhabits the shallows of the Rhotano Sea. Its barbed feelers are laced with a potent toxin that fells prey in an instant and, for some obscure reason that naturalists still struggle to ascertain, tints them a deep green.

51213.Name: Lodesmate's Pen
51213.Description: This specimen's name derives from its slender, cylindrical form, as well as several recorded instances of lodesmen losing their quills overboard and resorting to questionable measures to replace them. One has to pity the luckless wavekin hauled from the depths and subjected to multiple snout-first inkwell dippings.

51214.Name: Rhotano Roosterfish
51214.Description: This exceptionally aggressive wavekin is a common sight in the waters betwixt Thavnair and Eorzea. Some jokingly remark that its temperament must be learned from the pirates who ply their cutthroat trade in the region.

51232.Name: Palaka's Blade
51232.Description: The steely glint of this wavekin's dorsal fins evokes the weapons wielded by Thavnair's temple guardians. Perhaps it too watches over some sacred site in the depths.

51233.Name: Parjanya Wrasse
51233.Description: Long seen as harbingers of inclement weather, this wavekin's name approximates to “rain cloud” in the common tongue. While these fish do indeed tend to appear before storms hit, naturalists posit they are simply fleeing as fast as their little fins will carry them.

51234.Name: Simolestes
51234.Description: Though this leviathan is equipped with noteworthy jaws capable of shredding prey to pieces, this scalekin's name actually means “blunt-nosed thief.” Presumably this is a reference to it snatching the lives of any creatures foolish enough to contest its reign in the depths.

51215.Name: Rhotanosaurus
51215.Description: Unlike its mosasaur cousins that stalk the waters of inland Gyr Abania, this scalekin freely roams the realm's oceans. Despite presiding over a much larger habitat, its innate ferocity remains unchanged.

51216.Name: Royal Handmaiden
51216.Description: Legend has it that an envoy's attendant fell from their vessel while traversing the seas, whereupon they assumed a new, aquatic form beneath the waves─kimono transforming into scale, stitch by vibrant stitch.

51235.Name: Thavnasaurus
51235.Description: This ancient reptile inhabits the seas near Thavnair, where it enjoys enduring favor amongst the populace, appearing in folklore and myriad local tales. For despite its glistening maw of razor-sharp teeth, the Thavnasaurus has a remarkably gentle temperament.

51687.Name: Junior Jinbei
51687.Description: The calmest, most carefree inhabitant of Thavnairian coastal waters, this wavekin bears the markings of its approximate Hingan namesake: a breezy patterned garment traditionally worn during the warm summer months.

51218.Name: Frolicsome Fish
51218.Description: When these vibrantly striped wavekin were first spotted frolicking offshore by a group of island mammets, they bequeathed it with an intuitive─if not particularly inventive─name.

51238.Name: Silkfin
51238.Description: This subspecies is revered as a sign of good fortune in fishing villages across Thavnair. Its boldly patterned flanks are easily visible from above the water's surface, and sightings are said to precipitate a bumper catch for the day.

51219.Name: Captain's Finger
51219.Description: Of several species said to resemble a Roegadyn's formidable digits, these specimens are unquestionably the girthiest. Apparently, the creature's appellation is much to the chagrin of delicate-fingered nautical officers across the realm.

51220.Name: Bright Red Coral
51220.Description: This colony's brilliant red coloration stems from exposure to spectral currents, and sets it apart from other more muted coral species native to La Noscea. Equally brilliant is the price it commands at market stalls─though shoppers seeking trinkets might say “eye-watering” instead.

51221.Name: Royal Favorite
51221.Description: Tales speak of a royal attendant who plunged from their ship, only to transform into a resplendent wavekin in the inky depths. Some say they now ply the spectral currents with grace and determination, hoping to be reunited with their beloved former lord.

51222.Name: Pirate's Purse
51222.Description: Long associated with wealth and fortune, many believe this wavekin's raiment of gold-rimmed scales resembles a clutch of hoarded treasure.

51223.Name: Captain's Pen
51223.Description: Belonging to a species of wavekin that have the occasional misfortune of being used as writing implements, these specimens are noted for their impressive size. Presumably their indignation when being brandished as a pen is all the greater for this.

51224.Name: Tylosaurus
51224.Description: Deriving from its protruding cylindrical snout, this ancient scalekin's name roughly translates to “knobbed lizard.” Some specimens grow to such a colossal size that they are mistaken for whales.

51225.Name: Cieldalaes Roosterfish
51225.Description: This wide-roaming wavekin is frequently sighted riding spectral currents near the Cieldalaes, fluttering its spiny fins as if dancing to some distant rhythm.

51226.Name: Renegade Rhotanosaurus
51226.Description: This vicious monstrosity descends upon the spectral currents like a dread shadow, unassailable dominance secured with brutal strength and deadly fangs.

51227.Name: Red Boarfish
51227.Description: This wavekin's red, seedlike form conjures thoughts of abundance and plenty. For this reason, it is prized as a symbol of good fortune among spearfishers and divers alike.

51239.Name: Great Red Mantis
51239.Description: This variety of red mantis displays even more exuberant coloration than its cousins. Though this vivid hue dulls to an ash grey after cooking, the flesh remains simply scrumptious with a pinch of salt.

51240.Name: Guzel Gwl
51240.Description: Exposure to spectral currents seems to have further heightened this crustacean's already exceptional beauty─and taste. This pedigree is unambiguously reflected in its name: “resplendent rose,” as well as the fact it is routinely served at the satrap's palace.

51241.Name: Darpana
51241.Description: The distinct pattern adorning the scales of this flat fish resembles the glinting eye of some deep-sea behemoth. Indeed, the illusion is enough to send even wavekin much larger than darpana fleeing in terror.

51242.Name: Silverdart
51242.Description: When dried, these slender, sharp-nosed fish make for excellent projectiles. Some Thavnairian merchants have even taken to launching them at wall-mounted maps, planning their next excursion based on where the silver snout pierces the parchment. One wonders how many businesses have floundered as the result of an errant throw.

51243.Name: Satrapsaurus
51243.Description: Over the millennia, this ancient species has been much transformed by its time spent traversing spectral currents. In recent years, this specimen has garnered significant attention among Sharlayan scholars devoted to the study of underwater aetheric currents.

51244.Name: Tiger Mantis
51244.Description: Although large for mantis shrimp, these tiger-striped crustaceans are extremely timid. They spend much of their time cowering on the seabed, rarely moving unless swept up in a spectral current.

51245.Name: Mehi-mahi
51245.Description: This mahi-mahi subspecies moves at an infuriatingly ponderous pace. Seeking sport, some Thavnairian fishers will attempt to harry the creature along, though seldom to any avail. Apparently, even the sight of a fishing boat's prow bearing down upon it isn't enough to rouse a mehi-mahi from its leisurely locomotion.

51246.Name: Pliosaurus
51246.Description: This venerable scalekin is endowed with rows of saw-like teeth, which it uses to terrifying effect in dispatching hapless prey. Mere mention of its name─and the image of those dreadful fangs that inevitably follows─is enough to strike fear into the hearts of veteran fishers, and shred any confidence that mere ilms of timber might keep one safe from harm.

51217.Name: Spectral Starfish
51217.Description: Prolonged exposure to high concentrations of aether has partially crystallized these curious wavekin. They are frequently sighted at the forefront of spectral currents, calling to mind stars streaking across the firmament.

51237.Name: Spectral Grouper
51237.Description: The semi-crystalline flesh of this grouper results from absorbing a surfeit of aether over its lifespan─most of which it spends swimming at the vanguard of spectral currents.

51228.Name: Akupara
51228.Description: These sizable turtles traverse the seas with their shells held above the waves. Thus exposed to the elements, their carapaces become a rich tapestry of plant life, with the oldest specimens playing host to unique, highly complex ecosystems.

51247.Name: Manasvin
51247.Description: With an imposing name befitting a serpent possessing such massive saber-like tusks, Manasvin is heralded in the Near East as a warder of evil spirits─who are presumably as fearful of being skewered as any mortal would be.

52012.Name: Pote'uka
52012.Description: Named an “envoy of rainbows” in the Hanuhanu tongue, this fish gleams in seven distinct colors. Its scales are as popular as precious stones when it comes to decoration due to their brilliance and luster.

52013.Name: Harbor Cloud
52013.Description: Blooms of these jellyfish can be found off the docks of High Tide Harbor. When dried, their durability and elasticity make them valued packaging amongst traders.

52014.Name: Iq Ebaji
52014.Description: Exceedingly agile, this shrimp bears a name evocative of rust and deadly shears. Its tight ruddy-brown carapace conceals flesh bountiful in nourishment.

52015.Name: Yowekwa Inkhead
52015.Description: Squid native to the waters beneath Zorgor the Boundless. While the Tonawawta have used its ink as pigment since days of eld, its flesh is considered inedible by even the most ambitious epicureans.

52016.Name: Burst Lungfish
52016.Description: This remarkable species breathes by means of lungs, perhaps due to the shoals where it resides. Exhalations are summarily absorbed by the body, which creates enough carbonic acid to trigger a popping noise upon exposure to air.

52007.Name: Ner Lar Dor
52007.Description: This wavekin's vibrant flanks call to mind the iridescent strata of Worqor Lar Dor. Indeed, legend has it that the creature began life as a chunk of rock from that mighty edifice that plunged into a lake after being seized by sudden thirst.

52008.Name: Xehabopo'u
52008.Description: Rimed with algae and wreathed in foliage, this still, silent hunter lurks in the gloomy substrate of Miyakabek'zu. Intriguingly, the crystalline protrusions on its back share the same internal structure as many precious gems.

52009.Name: Skyfrond
52009.Description: While Eorzean eyes might associate this wavekin's rounded form with that of a heart, for the Mamool Ja, this revered creature is a symbol of the sky itself─a facet of the firmament glimpsed briefly through the swaying canopy above.

52010.Name: Rroneek Bichir
52010.Description: Some naturalists believe─against all evidence to the contrary─that rroneek are in fact a species of fish, and point to this ancient horned wavekin as some kind of progenitor. Regardless of one's thoughts on the matter, the creature's horns certainly evoke their land-dwelling namesake.

52297.Name: Great Ball of Lightning
52297.Description: Formed when lesser balls of lightning collide and fuse, these colossal, coruscating specimens are exceptionally volatile. The slightest rupture in its outer membrane can result in a catastrophic discharge of levin─a phenomenon which has left more than one curious naturalist frazzled...or worse.

52011.Name: Triple Threat
52011.Description: Endowed with three curving, scythe-like fins, this terrifying wavekin is the culmination of experiments to replicate an ancient sea monster. When its creators discovered it could cleave through electrope with unsettling ease, they began to regret their success.
